title: Respiratory and Circulatory Systems
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Respiratory and Circulatory Systems Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe the structure and function of the respiratory and circulatory systems and how they work together to supply the body with oxygen; describe how exercise affects heart and breathing rates. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Human Organ Systems)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on the lungs, heart, blood vessels, breathing, pulse and exercise. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The lungs take in oxygen; the heart pumps it around.
key_sub: Oxygen goes from the lungs into the blood, and the heart pumps the blood to every cell.
body_html:
How to think about it

The respiratory and circulatory systems work as a team.

  • Air goes in through the nose or mouth, down the windpipe and into the lungs.
  • In the lungs, oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.
  • The heart pumps blood through arteries (away from the heart) and veins (back to the heart).
  • Exercise makes the heart beat faster and breathing quicker, so muscles get more oxygen.
Example

Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?

arteries go away

veins come back

Answer: arteries

Example

Why does your pulse rise when you run?

muscles need more oxygen

Answer: the heart pumps faster

Common mistakes

  • Thinking we breathe out only carbon dioxide (we breathe out some oxygen too).
  • Mixing up arteries and veins.
  • Thinking the lungs pump blood.

faq.q: How do the lungs and heart work together?
faq.a: The lungs put oxygen into the blood. The heart pumps that blood to the body and brings blood back to the lungs.
A pulse is the beat of blood moving through an artery each time the heart pumps. You can feel it on your wrist or neck.

faq.q: How can we keep these systems healthy?
faq.a: Be active, do not smoke, eat well and avoid air pollution when you can.

items.q: On its way into the lungs, air passes through the nose or mouth. Where does it go next?
items.e: Nose or mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.

items.q: Which part of the gas exchange system is described here? “A sheet of muscle under the lungs that contracts and flattens when we breathe in.”
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: On its way into the lungs, air passes through a bronchiole. Where does it go next?
items.e: Nose or mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.

items.q: Which part of the gas exchange system is described here? “Tiny hairs on cells lining the airways that sweep mucus and dirt up and away from the lungs.”
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: When you breathe in, what happens to the intercostal muscles?
items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

items.q: Where does air come from just before it reaches an alveolus (air sac)?
items.e: Nose or mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.

items.q: What is the job of the alveoli?
c: Tiny air sacs where oxygen passes into the blood and carbon dioxide passes out.

Carries air from the throat to the bronchi and is held open by rings of cartilage.
Muscles between the ribs that move the ribcage up and out.
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: Why do doctors use a stethoscope?
c: to listen to the heart and lungs
items.e: Doctors listen for healthy sounds.

items.q: What is the job of the intercostal muscles?
c: Muscles between the ribs that move the ribcage up and out.
Carries air from the throat to the bronchi and is held open by rings of cartilage.
Two tubes that carry air from the trachea into each lung.
Small branching tubes that carry air to the alveoli.
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: When you breathe in, what happens to the ribcage?
items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

c: carry blood back to the heart
carry blood away from the heart
items.e: Veins return blood to the heart.

items.q: What does an asthma inhaler do?
c: It opens up the airways so air can flow more easily.
items.e: Medical technology helps people breathe.

items.q: When you breathe out, what happens to the diaphragm?
items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

items.q: When you breathe in, what happens to the diaphragm?
items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

items.q: Which part of the gas exchange system is described here? “Carries air from the throat to the bronchi and is held open by rings of cartilage.”
items.e: Each part has a job.

Carries air from the throat to the bronchi and is held open by rings of cartilage.
Muscles between the ribs that move the ribcage up and out.
Two tubes that carry air from the trachea into each lung.
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: What path does air take into the lungs?
c: nose or mouth → windpipe (trachea) → bronchi → lungs
items.e: Air travels down the windpipe.

items.q: When you breathe out, what happens to the intercostal muscles?
items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

items.q: Where does air come from just before it reaches the trachea (windpipe)?
items.e: Nose or mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.

items.q: What is the job of the diaphragm?
c: It moves down to help pull air into the lungs.
items.e: The diaphragm is a muscle under the lungs.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: letting oxygen and nutrients pass into the cells?
items.e: Capillaries: letting oxygen and nutrients pass into the cells.

items.q: Blood leaves the left side of the heart. Where does it go next?
c: the right side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: What is the main job of red blood cells?
c: carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body
letting oxygen and nutrients pass into the cells
items.e: Red blood cells: carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body?
items.e: Red blood cells: carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body.

items.q: Which part pumps blood around the body?
items.e: The heart pumps blood around the body.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: helping blood clot to stop bleeding?
items.e: Platelets: helping blood clot to stop bleeding.

items.q: Which part carries blood to and from all parts of the body?
items.e: The blood vessels carry blood to and from all parts of the body.

items.q: Which part is where oxygen passes into the blood?
items.e: The air sacs are where oxygen passes into the blood.

items.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
c: Your muscles need more oxygen, so blood must flow faster.
items.e: Exercise increases heart rate.

items.q: What is the main job of the lungs?
c: carrying blood away from the heart
carrying oxygen from the lungs to the body
letting oxygen and nutrients pass into the cells
giving the blood oxygen and taking away carbon dioxide
items.e: The lungs: giving the blood oxygen and taking away carbon dioxide.

items.q: Blood arrives at the left side of the heart. Where has it just come from?
c: the right side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: What is the function of the air sacs?
c: Are where oxygen passes into the blood.
Carries air from the nose to the lungs.
Take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.
Carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.
items.e: The air sacs are where oxygen passes into the blood.

items.q: Which organ systems work together to get oxygen to your muscles?
items.e: Lungs take in oxygen; blood carries it.

items.q: Blood leaves the body's organs and muscles. Where does it go next?
c: the right side of the heart
the left side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: Blood arrives at the lungs. Where has it just come from?
c: the right side of the heart
the left side of the heart
items.e: Body → right side of heart → lungs → left side of heart → body.

items.q: What is the function of the heart?
c: Are where oxygen passes into the blood.
Take in oxygen dissolved in water for fish.
Let gases enter and leave a plant.
items.e: The heart pumps blood around the body.

items.q: Which part carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells.

items.q: What do blood vessels called arteries do?
c: carry blood toward the heart only
carry blood away from the heart
items.e: Arteries carry blood away; veins bring it back.

items.q: Which part of the circulatory system has this job: carrying blood back to the heart?
items.e: Veins: carrying blood back to the heart.

items.q: The blood carries carbon dioxide. In which direction?
c: from the small intestine to all parts of the body
from the lungs to all parts of the body
from all parts of the body to the lungs
from the intestines to all parts of the body
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: Is blood in the left side of the heart rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Which gas does the body need from the air?
items.e: Cells use oxygen to release energy from food.

items.q: Is blood in the right side of the heart rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: How does smoking harm the respiratory system?
c: It makes the lungs bigger and healthier.
It damages the lungs so they take in less oxygen.
items.e: Smoke damages the air sacs.

items.q: Why does exhaled air make a cold mirror misty?
c: It is colder than the mirror.
It contains water vapour that condenses on the mirror.
items.e: We breathe out water vapour.

items.q: What is the pulse?
c: the beat felt at the wrist or neck when the heart pumps blood
items.e: Each pulse beat matches one heartbeat.

items.q: Is blood leaving the lungs rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Air we breathe in passes through the nose. Where does it go next?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: Is blood coming back from the body in the veins rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Air we breathe in passes through the windpipe. Where does it go next?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: Is blood in the arteries going to the leg muscles rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Is blood leaving a hard-working muscle rich in oxygen or low in oxygen?
c: it has no oxygen at all
items.e: Blood picks up oxygen in the lungs and gives it to the body's cells.

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from all parts of the body to the lungs?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: Air reaches the windpipe. Where did it come from just before?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: Where does oxygen pass into the blood?
items.e: Tiny air sacs in the lungs pass oxygen to the blood.

items.q: Which substance does the blood carry from the lungs to all parts of the body?
items.e: The blood carries oxygen, digested food and water to the cells, and carbon dioxide to the lungs.

items.q: The blood carries water. In which direction?
c: from the intestines to all parts of the body
from the small intestine to all parts of the body
from all parts of the body to the lungs
from the lungs to all parts of the body
items.e: The blood transports substances around the body.

items.q: What is the function of the circulatory system?
c: to transport substances such as oxygen and digested food around the body
items.e: The heart pumps blood through blood vessels.

items.q: Air reaches the air sacs. Where did it come from just before?
items.e: nose → windpipe → lungs → air sacs.

items.q: Arjun counts 60 pulse beats in 30 seconds. What is Arjun's pulse rate?
items.e: There are 2 lots of 30 seconds in a minute: 60 × 2 = 120.

items.q: What protects the lungs and heart?
items.e: The ribs form a cage around them.

items.q: Which statement about the heart is correct?
c: It is part of the respiratory system.
It takes in oxygen from the air.
It is a muscular organ that pumps blood all the time.
items.e: The heart never rests.

items.q: Why should the pulse be measured three times and the average found?
c: to make the heart beat faster
to make the result more reliable
items.e: Repeating reduces errors.

items.q: Why does the body need oxygen?
c: to release energy from digested food
items.e: Cells use oxygen and food to release energy.

items.q: Where is the heart found?
c: in the chest, between the lungs
items.e: The ribs protect the heart and lungs.

items.q: Maya measures a resting pulse three times: 74, 75, 73 beats per minute. What is the mean (average)?
items.e: Add them and divide by 3: 222 ÷ 3 = 74.

items.q: Which of these is carried by the blood?
items.e: Digested food is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

items.q: Olivia measures a resting pulse three times: 75, 69, 72 beats per minute. What is the mean (average)?
items.e: Add them and divide by 3: 216 ÷ 3 = 72.

items.q: Who first described how blood circulates around the body in 1628?
items.e: An English doctor.

items.q: Ethan counted his pulse for 15 seconds and got 20 beats. What is his pulse rate per minute?
Why should you measure your pulse three times and find the mean?
c: to make the result more reliable
because one reading is always wrong
to make the heart beat faster
items.e: Repeats reduce the effect of mistakes.

items.q: Olivia measures a resting pulse three times: 91, 92, 90 beats per minute. What is the mean (average)?
items.e: Add them and divide by 3: 273 ÷ 3 = 91.

items.q: Zoe measured her pulse at rest, then right after skipping for 2 minutes. Why did she measure it at rest first?
c: to compare the result after exercise with the normal rate
items.e: The resting rate is the control.

items.q: Which gas do we breathe out more of than we breathe in?
items.e: Cells make carbon dioxide as waste.

items.q: Which body systems work together to bring digested food to the muscles?
items.e: Food is digested and absorbed, then carried by the blood.

items.q: Why do fit people often have a lower resting pulse?
c: Their heart is stronger and pumps more blood with each beat.
items.e: Exercise strengthens the heart.

items.q: Why does a cut eventually stop bleeding?
items.e: Clotting forms a scab.

items.q: Noah measures a resting pulse three times: 75, 70, 74 beats per minute. What is the mean (average)?
items.e: Add them and divide by 3: 219 ÷ 3 = 73.

items.q: How long does it take for the pulse to return to resting after exercise? How could you find out?
c: Measure the pulse every minute after stopping until it matches the resting rate.
items.e: Plan a fair investigation.

items.q: Chloe bubbled her exhaled air through limewater and pumped room air through another tube of limewater. What did she find?
c: Only the limewater with exhaled air turned chalky quickly.
Both turned chalky at the same time.
Only the room air turned it chalky.
items.e: Exhaled air has more carbon dioxide.
